clues.text: This small town lies in a valley in the west of South Africa. Fruit farms and grape vines fill the valley round it.
clues.narrowing: rules out all places outside western South Africa

source.quote: Villiersdorp is a small town located in the Western Cape province of South Africa in the Overberg region, located near the Theewaterskloof Dam.

clues.text: Most farms round here grow wheat and canola crops. Since a huge dam was built, this valley changed, and its small local climate now suits fruit trees and grape vines best.
clues.narrowing: rules out the wheat valleys round it that have no dam-changed climate

source.quote: Unlike most of the geographical region which specialises in wheat and canola farming, the Villiersdorp Valley is now agriculturally and in micro-climate more similar to the Elgin Valley and Grabouw since the building of the Theewaterskloof Dam, and thus also specialises in deciduous fruit farming and viticulture.

clues.text: A local farmer set up this town in 1843. The town took its name from that same man.
clues.narrowing: rules out towns not founded by a local farmer in 1843

source.quote: The town is named after Field Cornet Pieter de Villiers, a local farmer who founded the settlement in 1843.

clues.text: This is the only place in the whole country that dries persimmons. The town co-op does this one rare job.
clues.narrowing: rules out every other town in the country

source.quote: The Villiersdorp Co-Op is also the only place in South Africa that processes and dries persimmons.

clues.text: A huge dam fills most of the valley floor by town. It is the biggest dam in its province, and it sends water to Cape Town.
clues.narrowing: confirms the town by the giant dam that fills its valley

source.quote: The Theewaterskloof Dam, the largest dam in the Western Cape and seventh largest in South Africa and important water supply to Cape Town fills the majority of the valley floor.

clues.text: This is a neighbourhood in the west part of Kamloops, in British Columbia, Canada. It sits just north of the Thompson River.
clues.narrowing: rules out everything outside western British Columbia

source.quote: Brocklehurst is a neighbourhood in the western area of Kamloops, British Columbia, Canada. Brocklehurst is bordered by the Thompson River to the south, North Shore to the east, Tranquille to the west, and the Batchelor hills and Batchelor Heights aka Batchelor Hills to the north.

clues.text: This is the warmest small climate spot in its city. It can be four degrees warmer than another part of the same city.
clues.narrowing: rules out the cooler parts of the same city

source.quote: The Brocklehurst area (or Brock, as referred to by its residents), is the warmest and most hospitable of the micro-climates in the city of Kamloops. There can be as much as a 4 degree Celsius increase from Brock to Aberdeen, all within the city of Kamloops.

clues.text: For a short time, it was a district town of its own. Then it joined Kamloops in 1973.
clues.narrowing: rules out neighbourhoods that did not join the city in 1973

source.quote: Brocklehurst, which briefly existed as a district municipality in its own right from 1971 until amalgamation with Kamloops in 1973, is the largest of the city's neighbourhoods, accounting for 16% of the city's population.

clues.text: It takes its name from a man from Liverpool, England. He lived here from 1896 to 1907.
clues.narrowing: rules out places not named for a Liverpool man who lived there

source.quote: The community is named after Ernest Brocklehurst, from Liverpool, England who lived in the area between 1896 and 1907.

clues.text: Look north from its streets to see the Batchelor Hills. They mark the top edge of this part of the city.
clues.narrowing: rules out parts of the city away from the northern hills

source.quote: Brocklehurst is bordered by the Thompson River to the south, North Shore to the east, Tranquille to the west, and the Batchelor hills and Batchelor Heights aka Batchelor Hills to the north.
